body:
## What to build

Preserve the scalar value of an admitted one-element character `.id` through empty rowwise nesting, including when the supplied string carries matrix or array dimensions.

Reproduced on main `59d55a7867ffc0255f75be32a233d9d475bcb7fb`: an empty input had one integer payload column, and `.id` was a one-by-one character matrix containing set. Scalar-string admission accepted it, as did `rlang::is_string()`. Both nesting verbs succeeded with the same identifier on a nonempty input. For the empty input, `nest_with_margins()` returned its documented zero outer rows, but `nest_by_with_margins()` failed while reconstructing its required one-row result: “Subscript must be a simple vector, not a matrix.” A one-element three-dimensional array failed analogously. Ordinary, named, and AsIs string controls succeeded. Local and dtplyr inputs reproduced the inconsistency.

Identifier normalization removed R names but retained dimensions. The empty rowwise reconstruction passed that remaining matrix/array directly to a selection helper, unlike the ordinary finalization path. The documented no-key empty-input result should contain one row, integer identifier 1, and one empty source cell. Closed #831 covered R names on scalar output arguments; this is the remaining dimension-attribute boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Empty no-key rowwise nesting with an admitted one-element matrix or array identifier produces the same result as its plain-string value: one row, integer identifier 1, and one zero-row nested cell.
- [ ] Cover local and dtplyr inputs and retain the identifier as a rowwise grouping key with the requested output column name.
- [ ] Preserve ordinary/named/AsIs controls, nonempty behavior, ungrouped nesting's zero-row behavior, and existing missing/empty/collision validation.
- [ ] A focused public-call regression demonstrates the attribute-dependent failure and succeeds after the repair.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Evidence

[Dated investigation and runnable reproductions](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/26f5c85e8e5783403d9fbadcfa3d1d9b9604b349/investigation/2026-10-29-nest-spec-dispatch-followup/README.md#f3-an-admitted-scalar-id-kept-its-dimensions-only-in-the-empty-fallback), recorded in PR #1005. The link is pinned to the evidence commit; the investigation did not implement the repair.

title: [P3] Preserve dimensional scalar identifiers in empty rowwise nesting
